refining.interpretation: Refined copper made from mined copper is the same metal one stage later, so the refining and mining series are never added. Because this series' basis and its treatment of feed are not stated, it is never set against demand and no refined balance is derived from it.

controls.label: Copper used in electric vehicles
controls.meaning: Copper the IEA counts in its Electric vehicles row for the year, world. It is not vehicle sales or the vehicle stock; the workbook does not say whether the row covers chargers.
controls.not_offered: Vehicles times copper per vehicle: neither is retained.

controls.label: Copper used in electricity networks
controls.meaning: The IEA Electricity networks row, world. The published wider direct current (DC) technology case is offered for the Stated Policies and High Demand scenarios; it has no Current Policies values.
controls.not_offered: Kilometres of line, grid spending or copper per kilometre: none is retained.

controls.label: Counted mine supply adjustment
controls.meaning: A change to the IEA's counted mine supply for the year: a signed change in kt, or a factor for one or more countries. Company disclosures are shown beside it as reference magnitudes, never as defaults.
controls.not_offered: Years of mine delay: no retained figure turns years into tonnes.

flags.hybrid: Hybrid: a component comes from another published scenario than the total it is applied to. This is not an IEA scenario; the IEA scenarios move together, and their published totals are shown beside it.
flags.technology_case: Published technology case: the networks value is the IEA's wider direct current (DC) technology case for the same scenario, applied to the base-case total.
flags.user_value: User value: a component was entered by the user, not taken from a publication.
flags.outside_published_spread: Outside all three IEA scenarios: an entered value lies outside the range of the three published scenario values for that row and year.
flags.reference_magnitude: Reference magnitude used as an assumption: a company disclosure, converted to copper tonnes, entered as a change in counted mine supply. It is not a projection.

capital_panel.rate_rule: A percentage of at least 0 and at most 100, with at most four decimals

producers.can_establish: For the year, each listed division's reported average revenue per pound exceeded its reported average unit net cash cost (by-product method): a statement about one year's division averages, each cost defined the company's way.
cannot_establish: Whether any mine is, or is not, at risk of closing. The test for a mine already built is whether price covers its avoidable cost, what it would stop paying if it stopped producing. These figures are not that cost: they average several mines, so the spread between mines is hidden; they follow each company's own definition, leaving some cash items out and including some costs that would not stop at once; they exclude sustaining capital; and their by-product credits move with other metals' prices.
Whether new supply gets built. A new mine must also cover sustaining capital, recover its initial capital with a return, and pay taxes and royalties, all spent years before its first tonne.
The industry's marginal cost: these are averages of large, long-life operations rich in by-products, not a sample of the industry.
Anything about how the companies' shares behave.
producers.brownfield_greenfield: A brownfield expansion uses an existing mine's permits, infrastructure and known ore, so its stated build time is short; the greenfield timelines in these filings run over many years, shaped by community agreements, water, power and security as much as by construction. Capital per tonne of annual capacity is therefore not comparable between them, and none is averaged or used as a default.

notes.incentive_break_even: The company used 'incentive copper price' in its 10-Ks and 'break-even economics' in the approval release. Neither term is defined in these documents; this project does not treat them as the same figure or derive one from the other.
notes.no_path: The company gives a first production target and a long-term annual rate, but no year-by-year path; nothing between them is shown or assumed.
